notes: Identity verified internally from the supplied canonical text: exact article title, Jason A Okonofua, David Paunesku, Gregory M Walton, PNAS 2016;113(19):5221–5226 and DOI 10.1073/pnas.1523698113 match the neutral original reference. This is a PMC full primary article parse (PMCID PMC4868443), with results, Methods, tables, and embedded SI, not an abstract-only excerpt or secondary report. No supplied PDF; page layout could not be checked. Target ambiguity: the supplied study number 2 and p. 2 do not uniquely establish an outcome; Experiment 2 reports two distinct direct effects. Candidate respect: printed d = 2.42, t(300) = 20.98, P < 0.001. Candidate anticipated motivation to behave well: printed d = 0.40, t(300) = 3.43, P < 0.001. Figure 1 explicitly gives n = 302 college students for Experiment 2; no exclusion account identified for that experiment. The description instead concerns Experiment 3 suspension rates: primary printed OR = 0.42, z = –3.33, P = 0.001; adjusted OR = 0.49, z = –2.37, P = 0.018. Preserve OR as printed; no conversion to d. Methods explicitly identifies primary analytic n = 1,682 student participants nested within school, teacher and classroom, with 31 randomized teachers; 2,069 school records supplied and 387 excluded (172 not taught by a randomized teacher; 215 lacked matched prior/current discipline records). Three further students missing gender are omitted from adjusted analyses, explicitly n = 1,679. These are candidates only; no candidate N promoted to a verified target N. No N derived from df or group sums. Replication, original p, and success were unassigned and remain placeholders.
